units.rhetorical_move: diagnoses Earth before offering Mars
units.function: list the failures, then the chance to start over

original_instantiations: three named failures plague civilization on Earth
a new planet is then offered as a fresh start

units.source_excerpt: Civilization on Earth is plagued with three named failures, and a new planet offers a fresh start.
units.reusable_pattern: Open by diagnosing the present, then offer the blank start.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the diagnosis.

units.rhetorical_move: borrows a named earthly model
units.function: say which real system the policy copies

original_instantiations: the income policy copies one named earthly model
a minimum wage and a capped tax come out of it

units.source_excerpt: We implemented one named earthly model and derived a wage and a capped tax from it.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the real-world system a policy is copied from.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the borrowed model as original.

units.rhetorical_move: reports a coefficient falling from one value to another
units.function: give the before and the after

original_instantiations: one inequality coefficient falls from a stated value
it lands near the level of the borrowed model

units.source_excerpt: We reduced one inequality coefficient from a higher stated value to a lower one.
units.reusable_pattern: Report an improvement as a from-to pair.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not give only the ending value.

units.rhetorical_move: ranks disciplines against espoused values
units.function: score options by stated values

original_instantiations: disciplines are ranked by how they serve stated values
the values are called espoused

units.source_excerpt: We ranked disciplines by how much they contribute to our espoused values.
units.reusable_pattern: Score options against values the paper calls espoused.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not rename espoused.

units.rhetorical_move: numbers three long-run discoveries
units.function: deliver findings as a numbered list

original_instantiations: the findings are numbered one, two and three
each number holds one discovery

units.source_excerpt: We discovered three things and numbered them.
units.reusable_pattern: Deliver long-run findings as a numbered list.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge two numbers.

units.rhetorical_move: concedes the colony may differ from Earth
units.function: limit the model by the unprecedented setting

original_instantiations: the colony is called unprecedented
it may show traits no known society has

units.source_excerpt: The colony is unprecedented and may differ from every society we know.
units.reusable_pattern: Concede that an unprecedented setting may break the model.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the model transfers unchanged.

units.rhetorical_move: names the governing body
units.function: brand the institution

original_instantiations: the governing body gets a coined hyphenated name
it taxes progressively to fund equity

units.source_excerpt: The proposal gives the governing body a coined hyphenated name.
units.reusable_pattern: Brand an institution with a coined name.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not expand the coined name.

units.rhetorical_move: guarantees a livable salary
units.function: promise necessities and comforts

original_instantiations: participants are guaranteed a salary
the salary covers necessities and comforts

units.source_excerpt: Participants are guaranteed a salary covering fundamental necessities and comforts.
units.reusable_pattern: State a guarantee and name what it covers.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the comforts.

units.rhetorical_move: calls education of the upmost importance
units.function: use the nonstandard superlative

original_instantiations: education is called of the upmost importance
the reason is that the pioneers will die off

units.source_excerpt: Education is of the upmost importance because the pioneers eventually die off.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the nonstandard superlative when stressing one thing.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct upmost to utmost when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: defines equality against equity
units.function: split two near-synonyms

original_instantiations: equality is defined as equal outcomes
equity is defined as fair outcomes from equal treatment

units.source_excerpt: We define equality as equal outcomes and equity as fair outcomes.
units.reusable_pattern: Define two near-synonyms separately so they do not collapse.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the two terms interchangeably.

units.rhetorical_move: offers three production options
units.function: list the ways a citizen may contribute

original_instantiations: three production options are listed
each mixes working with learning

units.source_excerpt: Citizens choose among three production options, each mixing work and learning.
units.reusable_pattern: List the allowed options and count them.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fourth option.

units.rhetorical_move: restates the three shortcomings
units.function: name what the model improves

original_instantiations: the model focuses on three named shortcomings
each shortcoming gets its own sub-model

units.source_excerpt: Our model focuses on improving three named shortcomings.
units.reusable_pattern: State the scope as the shortcomings being improved.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fourth shortcoming.

units.rhetorical_move: says the policies were checked for viability
units.function: verify the parts against each other

original_instantiations: the separate models are incorporated together
the combination checks economic viability

units.source_excerpt: We incorporated the separate models to verify that the policies are economically viable.
units.reusable_pattern: Say the parts were combined in order to check viability.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim viability without the check.

units.rhetorical_move: sets thresholds that diminish
units.function: show returns falling as credentials rise

original_instantiations: each credential gets a human-capital threshold
the gaps between thresholds shrink

units.source_excerpt: The thresholds rise with each credential, but the gaps shrink.
units.reusable_pattern: Show diminishing returns by shrinking gaps between thresholds.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not space the thresholds evenly.

units.rhetorical_move: assumes identical income curves
units.function: justify an equality assumption

original_instantiations: male and female income curves are assumed identical
the reason is that unequal policy breeds tension

units.source_excerpt: We assume identical income curves, because unequal policy leads to societal tension.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify an equality assumption by the tension it avoids.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the assumption as a finding.

units.rhetorical_move: weighs two factors for the age mix
units.function: name the factors behind a choice

original_instantiations: two factors decide the age distribution
sustainability is the first of them

units.source_excerpt: We considered two factors when selecting the age distribution.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the factors behind a design choice and count them.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a third factor.

units.rhetorical_move: assumes migrants drop their stereotypes
units.function: state a behavioral assumption

original_instantiations: migrants are assumed to set their stereotypes aside
they are also assumed to act in their best long-term interest

units.source_excerpt: We assume migrants set aside their stereotypes and act in their long-term interest.
units.reusable_pattern: State a behavioral assumption in the migrants' own terms.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the assumption as observed.

units.rhetorical_move: doubts that equilibrium can hold
units.function: concede isolation breaks equilibrium

original_instantiations: true equilibrium may prove impossible
the cause is isolation from other civilizations

units.source_excerpt: It may prove impossible to maintain true equilibrium, given the isolation.
units.reusable_pattern: Concede that isolation may make equilibrium impossible.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assert equilibrium anyway.

units.rhetorical_move: fits an inverse curve
units.function: name the curve used

original_instantiations: incomes are drawn from an inverse curve
the curve comes from the earlier income model

units.source_excerpt: Random incomes were generated from the inverse distribution curve.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the distribution incomes are drawn from.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not substitute a different distribution.

units.rhetorical_move: compares two costs with an inequality
units.function: frame a decision as one cost against another

original_instantiations: childcare cost is set against opportunity cost
the larger one decides the exit

units.source_excerpt: The decision compares the cost of childcare with the opportunity cost.
units.reusable_pattern: Frame a decision as a comparison of two named costs.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a third cost.

units.rhetorical_move: runs a Monte Carlo of couples
units.function: state the draw count and who is drawn

original_instantiations: several thousand random couples are drawn
couples with and without children are both included

units.source_excerpt: A Monte Carlo drew several thousand random couples, with and without children.
units.reusable_pattern: State a simulation as a draw count plus who is drawn.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not change the draw count.

units.rhetorical_move: says the model is most sensitive to three things
units.function: name the sensitive inputs

original_instantiations: three inputs dominate the sensitivity
childcare cost is the first of them

units.source_excerpt: The model is most sensitive to childcare cost, fertility, and the minimum wage.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the inputs a model is most sensitive to.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add an input not named.

units.rhetorical_move: explains a rise by a missing age band
units.function: give the cause of a transient

original_instantiations: the ratios rise over the first years
the cause is a missing band of young children

units.source_excerpt: The ratios rise at first because one age band of children is missing, then stabilize.
units.reusable_pattern: Explain a transient by the group that is missing.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the rise unexplained.

units.rhetorical_move: poses the tax rise as a rhetorical question
units.function: argue by asking

original_instantiations: doubling the population is met with a question
the question asks whether the tax must double too

units.source_excerpt: Must the tax rise to its limit if the population doubles, and what would then incentive work?
units.reusable_pattern: Argue a point by asking a question the reader answers no to.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not answer the question in the same sentence.

units.rhetorical_move: keeps a wrong verb
units.function: leave the grammar error in place

original_instantiations: incentive is used where incentivize belongs
the sentence is otherwise a rhetorical question

units.source_excerpt: The question uses incentive as a verb.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep a wrong verb when it marks the writer's voice.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct the verb when quoting.

units.rhetorical_move: says the utopia would break down
units.function: name the vision and its failure

original_instantiations: the colony is given a coined name
its utopian vision breaks down either way

units.source_excerpt: Either way, the vision of the coined colony as a utopia would quickly break down.
units.reusable_pattern: End a dilemma by saying the vision breaks down either way.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not offer a third way.

units.rhetorical_move: reports human capital falling then rising
units.function: give the dip and the recovery

original_instantiations: human capital falls at first as the founders die
it later rises from returns on education

units.source_excerpt: Human capital first decreases as the founders die, then increases from educational returns.
units.reusable_pattern: Report a result as a fall followed by a rise, with a cause for each.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report only the rise.

units.rhetorical_move: warns that the wrong migrants undo the policy
units.function: name what an undesired input offsets

original_instantiations: undesired migrant distributions offset the equality
the offset undoes what the policies seek

units.source_excerpt: Undesired distributions could offset the equality the policies seek to establish.
units.reusable_pattern: Warn that the wrong input offsets the policy's goal.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim robustness against every distribution.

units.rhetorical_move: attributes oscillations to the schedule
units.function: name the cause of a cycle

original_instantiations: the age distribution oscillates
scheduled migrations from Earth cause the oscillation

units.source_excerpt: Oscillations in the age distribution come from the scheduled migrations.
units.reusable_pattern: Attribute a cycle to the schedule that drives it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the oscillation noise.

units.rhetorical_move: reduces the crisis to two choices
units.function: state a dilemma

original_instantiations: the government must raise the tax or cut spending
both choices are then examined

units.source_excerpt: The government must choose one of two choices: raise the tax or cut spending per head.
units.reusable_pattern: Reduce a crisis to exactly two choices.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a third choice.

units.rhetorical_move: claims separation let each sector be optimized
units.function: defend solving the parts apart

original_instantiations: the three problems were approached separately
none of the resulting policies compromise each other

units.source_excerpt: Approaching the problems separately let us optimize each sector without compromise.
units.reusable_pattern: Defend a separation by saying the parts do not compromise each other.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the separation was costless beyond the text.

units.rhetorical_move: says the model develops over time
units.function: claim the design is scalable

original_instantiations: the model is called relatively scalable
it is designed to develop over decades

units.source_excerpt: The model is relatively scalable and designed to develop over time.
units.reusable_pattern: Claim scalability and name the horizon it develops over.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the hedge relatively.

units.rhetorical_move: admits there is no unifying variable
units.function: name the three incompatible units

original_instantiations: the three models use three different units
no single variable connects them

units.source_excerpt: One flaw is the lack of a unifying variable connecting the three models.
units.reusable_pattern: Admit the parts are not joined, and name what each uses.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent the unifying variable.

units.rhetorical_move: rejects the unifying variable as arbitrary
units.function: say why the obvious fix was declined

original_instantiations: a unifying variable was considered
it was declined because the relations felt arbitrary

units.source_excerpt: We could have used one key variable, but felt the relations would be too arbitrary.
units.reusable_pattern: Say a fix was considered and why it was declined.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the declined fix as done.

units.rhetorical_move: says utopias do not last
units.function: ground the data gap in history

original_instantiations: isolated societies rarely last long
so data on them has always been scarce

units.source_excerpt: There has long been a lack of data on isolated societies, since they do not tend to last long.
units.reusable_pattern: Explain a data gap by the history that caused it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim data the text says is missing.

units.rhetorical_move: lists three future steps
units.function: keep the future work concrete

original_instantiations: three future steps are listed
the last is a contingency plan for mass migration

units.source_excerpt: For future research we list three concrete steps, ending with contingency plans.
units.reusable_pattern: List future work as concrete steps, not themes.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a fourth step.

units.rhetorical_move: drops a letter from a month
units.function: leave the citation typo

original_instantiations: one access date drops a letter from the month
the citation otherwise follows the list's format

units.source_excerpt: One access date spells the month without its first letter.
units.reusable_pattern: Keep a citation's dropped letter unrepaired.
prohibited_generalizations: The typo belongs to this reference list and does not transfer.

units.rhetorical_move: prints the decision matrix as a grid of decimals
units.function: let the weights stand as numbers

original_instantiations: the matrix gives a decimal weight per cell
rows are disciplines and columns are values

units.source_excerpt: The appendix prints a decision matrix of decimal weights.
units.reusable_pattern: Present a weighting as a grid of decimals.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not round the printed weights.

units.rhetorical_move: breaks a row label across the margin
units.function: keep the clipped heading

original_instantiations: a row label is cut off at the left margin
only the tail of the phrase survives

units.source_excerpt: One row label is clipped at the left margin.
units.reusable_pattern: Leave a clipped label as it prints.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reconstruct the clipped words.

units.rhetorical_move: refers the reader to a named appendix
units.function: point at supplementary material by code

original_instantiations: a figure is deferred to a coded appendix
the code mixes letters and a digit

units.source_excerpt: Sample findings are deferred to an appendix identified by a short code.
units.reusable_pattern: Point the reader to an appendix by its code.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not rename the appendix.
